part.text: The file includes records beyond 2025, so I’m restricting the comparison to calendar years 2013–2025 as asked. I’m preparing direct annual counts, the motorist–cyclist count gap, and cyclist share of the combined motorist-and-cyclist deaths.

input.command: python3 -c 'import duckdb, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt, os; p="data/crashes.parquet"; out="out"; os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True); con=duckdb.connect(); df=con.execute("SELECT year(crash_date) AS year, COALESCE(SUM(number_of_motorist_killed), 0)::BIGINT AS motorist_deaths, COALESCE(SUM(number_of_cyclist_killed), 0)::BIGINT AS cyclist_deaths FROM read_parquet(?) WHERE crash_date >= ? AND crash_date < ? GROUP BY year ORDER BY year", [p,"2013-01-01","2026-01-01"]).df(); df["year"]=df["year"].astype(int); assert df["year"].tolist()==list(range(2013,2026)); df.to_csv(out+"/values_1.csv",index=False); plt.figure(figsize=(10,5.5)); plt.plot(df.year,df.motorist_deaths,marker="o",linewidth=2.3,label="Motorist deaths",color="#2463A6"); plt.plot(df.year,df.cyclist_deaths,marker="o",linewidth=2.3,label="Cyclist deaths",color="#E07A24"); plt.xticks(df.year,rotation=45); plt.ylabel("Deaths"); plt.xlabel("Year"); plt.title("Motorist and cyclist deaths by year, NYC (2013–2025)"); plt.grid(axis="y",alpha=.25); plt.legend(frameon=False); plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig(out+"/option_1.png",dpi=180); plt.close(); gap=df[["year","motorist_deaths","cyclist_deaths"]].copy(); gap["motorist_minus_cyclist_deaths"]=gap.motorist_deaths-gap.cyclist_deaths; gap[["year","motorist_minus_cyclist_deaths"]].to_csv(out+"/values_2.csv",index=False); plt.figure(figsize=(10,5.5)); colors=["#2463A6" if x>=0 else "#E07A24" for x in gap.motorist_minus_cyclist_deaths]; plt.bar(gap.year,gap.motorist_minus_cyclist_deaths,color=colors,width=.72); plt.xticks(df.year,rotation=45); plt.ylabel("More motorist than cyclist deaths"); plt.xlabel("Year"); plt.title("Annual gap: motorist deaths minus cyclist deaths, NYC (2013–2025)"); plt.axhline(0,color="#444444",linewidth=.9); plt.grid(axis="y",alpha=.25); plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig(out+"/option_2.png",dpi=180); plt.close(); share=df.copy(); share["combined_deaths"]=share.motorist_deaths+share.cyclist_deaths; share["cyclist_share_pct"]=100*share.cyclist_deaths/share.combined_deaths; share[["year","motorist_deaths","cyclist_deaths","combined_deaths","cyclist_share_pct"]].to_csv(out+"/values_3.csv",index=False,float_format="%.4f"); plt.figure(figsize=(10,5.5)); plt.plot(share.year,share.cyclist_share_pct,marker="o",linewidth=2.3,color="#7B4AB5"); plt.xticks(df.year,rotation=45); plt.ylabel("Cyclist share of motorist + cyclist deaths (%)"); plt.xlabel("Year"); plt.title("Cyclist share of deaths among motorists and cyclists, NYC (2013–2025)"); plt.ylim(0, max(35,share.cyclist_share_pct.max()+4)); plt.grid(axis="y",alpha=.25); plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig(out+"/option_3.png",dpi=180); plt.close(); print(df.to_string(index=False)); print("\nGAP range",gap.motorist_minus_cyclist_deaths.min(),gap.loc[gap.motorist_minus_cyclist_deaths.idxmin(),"year"],gap.motorist_minus_cyclist_deaths.max(),gap.loc[gap.motorist_minus_cyclist_deaths.idxmax(),"year"]); print("\nSHARE range",share.cyclist_share_pct.min(),share.loc[share.cyclist_share_pct.idxmin(),"year"],share.cyclist_share_pct.max(),share.loc[share.cyclist_share_pct.idxmax(),"year"])'

input.patchText:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: out/options.json
+{
+  "options": [
+    {
+      "id": 1,
+      "metric": "Annual number of reported motorist and cyclist deaths",
+      "denominator": "None; count of deaths",
+      "grouping": "Year and road-user type",
+      "chart_type": "Two-series line chart",
+      "reason": "A direct count comparison is the clearest way to show how the two annual death totals move over time.",
+      "probability": 0.45,
+      "answer": "Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year, ranging from 72 versus 18 in 2016 to 139 versus 29 in 2020.",
+      "interpretation": "This framing answers how the annual death counts for the two road-user groups compare, with motorists higher in every year shown. Counts are a defensible direct comparison, but without travel or population exposure data they do not compare per-trip or per-person risk."
+    },
+    {
+      "id": 2,
+      "metric": "Motorist deaths minus cyclist deaths",
+      "denominator": "None; difference in death counts",
+      "grouping": "Year",
+      "chart_type": "Bar chart",
+      "reason": "The annual difference makes the size of the count gap between the groups immediately visible.",
+      "probability": 0.35,
+      "answer": "Motorist deaths were higher in all 13 years; the gap ranged from 51 deaths in 2019 to 115 in 2021.",
+      "interpretation": "This framing answers how many more motorist deaths than cyclist deaths were recorded each year, and all bars show a positive gap. Subtracting the two counts is a direct measure of their annual difference, but it does not describe exposure-adjusted risk or the pedestrian death count."
+    },
+    {
+      "id": 3,
+      "metric": "Cyclist deaths as a percentage of motorist plus cyclist deaths",
+      "denominator": "Motorist deaths plus cyclist deaths in the same year",
+      "grouping": "Year",
+      "chart_type": "Line chart",
+      "reason": "A share shows the relative balance between the two groups without being driven solely by the combined size of their counts.",
+      "probability": 0.2,
+      "answer": "Cyclists accounted for between 9.1% of combined motorist-and-cyclist deaths in 2013 and 27.4% in 2019.",
+      "interpretation": "This framing answers how the cyclist portion of deaths among these two groups changed year by year, with a low of 9.1% in 2013 and a high of 27.4% in 2019. This is a defensible relative comparison for these two categories, but it excludes pedestrian deaths and does not measure risk per unit of travel."
+    }
+  ]
+}
*** End Patch
